flow: Customer Web Browser -> Web/API Server (QuickCart App) (Login credentials, browsing/checkout requests)
description: An attacker could spoof a legitimate Customer Web Browser by stealing or guessing credentials used in the flow to Web/API Server (QuickCart App), impersonating a real user or admin.
mitigation: Enforce MFA for admin and customer accounts, use short-lived signed session tokens, rate-limit login attempts, and bind sessions to device/IP heuristics.

flow: Customer Web Browser -> Web/API Server (QuickCart App) (Login credentials, browsing/checkout requests)
description: Sensitive data (Login credentials, browsing/checkout requests) flowing between Customer Web Browser and Web/API Server (QuickCart App) could be exposed via interception, misconfigured access controls, or verbose logging/error messages.
mitigation: Encrypt sensitive data at rest and in transit, apply least-privilege DB access, never store raw payment data (use the gateway's tokenization), and scrub PII from logs and error messages.

flow: Customer Web Browser -> Web/API Server (QuickCart App) (Login credentials, browsing/checkout requests)
description: Web/API Server (QuickCart App) is reachable from Customer Web Browser and could be overwhelmed by high-volume or malformed requests (e.g., credential-stuffing bursts, large payloads).
mitigation: Apply rate limiting / WAF rules at the perimeter, use CAPTCHA after repeated failures, set request size limits, and enable autoscaling with circuit breakers.

flow: Admin Staff Browser -> Internal Admin Panel (Admin login, inventory edits, order lookups)
description: Data in transit or at rest between Admin Staff Browser and Internal Admin Panel (Admin login, inventory edits, order lookups) could be tampered with if integrity controls (TLS, signed requests, DB constraints) are weak.
mitigation: Use TLS 1.2+ everywhere, validate/sanitize all inputs server-side, apply parameterized queries, and enforce DB-level constraints and request signing for admin writes.

flow: Admin Staff Browser -> Internal Admin Panel (Admin login, inventory edits, order lookups)
description: A regular authenticated user, or an attacker who compromises Admin Staff Browser, could attempt to reach Internal Admin Panel and perform admin-only actions if authorization checks are missing or inconsistently enforced server-side.
mitigation: Enforce server-side authorization checks (not just UI hiding) on every admin endpoint, use role-based access control, and isolate the admin panel on a separate network path with its own auth.

description: A user or admin could deny having performed an action affecting Login credentials, browsing/checkout requests if Web/API Server (QuickCart App) does not keep tamper-evident audit logs tied to an identity.
